title: Shards of Nine Honks
logline: Eight honks scatter. The ninth was never sounded; its shard is the egg, and it warms.
epigraph: A broadcast that breaks is still a map of who was listening.
description: Chapter 9 of Lore.Land: Shards of Nine Honks. Signal fragments across the night. Collecting them is craft, not compulsion. The missing ninth is the egg — the kernel of a call that was never blown.

children.text: before it was a skyline. Eight shards of a broken honk lay in an arc, each one a relic of a call that had reached someone. The pieces rearranged with every step Boof took. The ninth place in the arc was empty until she set the egg there. It fitted. It warmed. The ninth honk had never been sounded; its shard had been a cell all along.

content.text: The puzzle was incomplete on purpose. No single keeper can hold the whole call. "Solve this," a voice whispered, "if you can." Solving was the wrong verb. Seeing the kernel was enough: eight receipts of listening, one unreceipted heat.
"It’s not about solving, Boof," the Fool’s voice whispered, "it’s about seeing which shard was never a horn."

img.alt: Eight glowing shards of a broken horn on a night ridge; the ninth shard is the coal-dark cracked egg at the center.

sections.figcaption: Nine honks: eight relics, one kernel that was never blown.

content.text: Boof knelt among the shards. Some fitted. Others refused, as if the call itself resisted a single owner. Scattering forces community: no one clerk can hold the whole broadcast. The egg in the ninth place was the kernel of the call — the small constitution of a sound that had chosen heat instead of air. She left the eight where they lay, for whoever had been listening, and carried the ninth toward Bone.land, where structure would have to hold.

content.text: "How can I solve this if I don’t know what it is?" Boof murmured. She did not need the full picture. She needed the kernel, and she was already carrying it.
